channel.title: AI | Fred Xu
channel.description: Essays on AI and what it changes in learning, work and university life, many of them drawn from my lecture series on LLMs and AI agents.

item.title: Improving Function Space Flow Matching with Kernel Optimal Transport
item.description: kFFM replaces the random noise–data pairing of Functional Flow Matching with entropic optimal transport under a kernel-induced cost, the coupling behind the Hilbert Sinkhorn Divergence: a signature kernel for paths, a Sobolev or Euclidean RBF for fields. Same network, same loss, 5–7% more training time, and better samples on eight time-series and PDE benchmarks.

item.title: Graph Anomaly Detection as Finite-Horizon Control
item.description: EB-GAD scores graph anomalies with no labels and no training: empirical Bayes fits a graph-aware Gaussian model of normal in closed form, and each node is scored by the finite-horizon control energy needed to steer a neutral start to it under a graph Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process. Best or tied-best AUROC on 9 of 11 benchmarks.

item.title: A Unified Uncertainty Representation for Graph Neural Networks
item.description: DSS-GNN stores each node's embedding as a short polynomial chaos expansion in one shared Gaussian variable and filters it along two spectral axes, graph frequency and chaos order. Readouts of this one representation, computed in a single deterministic pass, give calibrated predictions, OOD scores and robustness to distribution shift.

item.title: The Virtue of Friction
item.description: Some friction only wastes our time, and some is how understanding is built and how hard work becomes absorbing. On learning, skill and flow when a machine can do the work.
